identity.title: Sub-kiloparsec ALMA Imaging of Compact Star-forming Galaxies at z ~ 2.5: Revealing the Formation of Dense Galactic Cores in the Progenitors of Compact Quiescent Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present spatially-resolved Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) 870 $\mu$m dust continuum maps of six massive, compact, dusty star-forming galaxies (SFGs) at $z\sim2.5$.

targets.name: 6 compact SFGs in CANDELS GOODS-S (incl. GDS-9834, GDS-11701, GDS-3280)

evidence.quote: The 6 galaxies analyzed in this paper are drawn from the sample of compact SFGs in the CANDELS ((cite: candelsgro)) GOODS-S region presented in (cite: barro14a).

question.value: Where is star formation occurring relative to the stellar mass in compact star-forming galaxies at z~2.5, and does this support dissipative formation of compact quiescent galaxies?

evidence.quote: direct measurements of their spatial distribution of the star formation relative to the mass profile, needed to discriminate between the two formation scenarios discussed above, are still inconclusive.

claims.hypothesis: Compact SFGs have nuclear starbursts more concentrated than their stellar mass
claims.experiment: Joint ALMA 870um and HST profile fitting for 6 galaxies
claims.result: Mean SFR profile ~1.5x more concentrated than stellar mass; FIR sizes ~1.9x smaller than optical

evidence.loc: Stellar mass, UV- and IR- SFR surface density profiles
evidence.quote: The average (UV+IR) SFR profile is approximately $1.5\times$ more concentrated than the average stellar mass profile

claims.hypothesis: Dissipative nuclear starbursts form dense cores
claims.experiment: Evolve mass profile with constant SFR profile for 200 Myr
claims.finding: Supports dissipation-driven formation of compact quiescent galaxies

evidence.quote: The strong nuclear starbursts embedded in larger stellar mass profiles found in compact SFGs are indeed an excellent match to the dissipation-driven scenario.

limitations_admitted.value: Profiles detected only to r~3-4 kpc; larger radii rely on Sersic fits

evidence.loc: Stellar mass, UV- and IR- SFR surface density profiles
evidence.quote: Therefore, the results at larger radii are based on the best-fit Sérsic profiles.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 6 galaxies, selected to be FIR bright
Evolution assumes constant SFR profile and no mergers or outflows
Dust-continuum size equated with SFR distribution
Gas masses rely on assumed gas-to-dust ratio
Discrepancy between the 200 Myr used in text and Δt=±100 Myr in abstract

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB raw for 6 targets in two executions
reproducibility.score_reason: Public ALMA project code and clear overall recipe, but imaging and fitting details are sparse (letter format).
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key results depend on HST/Herschel ancillary data and many unspecified fitting choices.
